- [S1] Ministry of Education, Singapore (CPDD), Science Teaching & Learning Syllabus, Primary Three to Six, Standard / Foundation (implementation from the 2023 Primary Three cohort; cover updated January 2026). Page 38, Diversity of Living and Non-Living Things (General characteristics and classification), Primary 3: describe the characteristics of living things (need water, food and air to survive; grow, respond and reproduce); recognise some broad groups of living things: plants (flowering, non-flowering), animals (amphibians, birds, fish, insects, mammals, reptiles), fungi (mould, mushroom, yeast) and bacteria; observe living and non-living things and infer differences; classify living things into broad groups (in plants and animals) based on common observable characteristics; show curiosity, and care and concern for living things. Note: recall of names of specific living things (e.g., guppy) and their characteristics (e.g., give birth to young alive) is not required. Page 42: the Primary 3 life cycles topic names the chicken, cockroach, frog, grasshopper, beetle, butterfly and mosquito. Page 43: Primary 5 investigates the ways plants reproduce (spores, seeds). Pages 82–83, glossary: classify, to group objects or events based on common characteristics; recognise, to identify facts, characteristics or concepts critical to understanding. / 新加坡教育部课程规划与发展司，《小学三至六年级科学教学大纲（标准 / 基础）》（2023 年小三学生起实施，封面 2026 年 1 月更新）。第 38 页“生物与非生物的多样性（一般特征与分类）”，小三：描述生物的特征（需要水、食物和空气才能生存；会生长、反应和繁殖）；认出生物的几个大类：植物（开花、不开花）、动物（两栖动物、鸟类、鱼类、昆虫、哺乳动物、爬行动物）、真菌（霉菌、蘑菇、酵母）和细菌；观察生物与非生物，推断它们的不同；按共同的、看得见的特征把生物分成大组（植物和动物）；表现出好奇心，爱护生物。注：不要求记住具体生物的名称（如孔雀鱼）和它们的特征（如胎生）。第 42 页：小三“生活周期”点名鸡、蟑螂、蛙、蝗虫、甲虫、蝴蝶、蚊子。第 43 页：小五探究植物繁殖的方式（孢子、种子）。第 82–83 页词汇表：分类（classify），按共同的特征把物体或事件分组；认出（recognise），辨认出对理解一件事至关重要的事实、特征或概念。 (Read 2026-10-21 (page numbers are those printed at the foot; printed page n is PDF page n + 1). The page lists the needs and the three processes only: moving about is not on the Singapore list. / 2026-10-21 读取（页码是页脚印的数字；印的第 n 页是 PDF 第 n + 1 页）。这一页只列需要的东西和三种生命过程，“会动”不在新加坡的单子上。) — https://www.moe.gov.sg/api/media/ba3562d3-5b31-4459-8693-45cde7b97273/Primary-Science-Syllabus-2023_May24.pdf
- [S2] Geniebook, Diversity of Animals (Primary 3 Science): mammals have hair and breathe with lungs, feed their young on milk, and most give birth to young alive; birds have feathers, a beak, a pair of wings and a pair of legs, and lay hard-shelled eggs, and ostriches and penguins cannot fly; fish have scales, fins and a tail and breathe through gills, and most lay eggs; amphibians have moist skin; reptiles have dry skin with scales and breathe with lungs, and some, such as turtles, have a shell; an insect has three body parts, six legs and two feelers and a hard exoskeleton; practice in flowcharts, choosing headings for groups and finding animals classified wrongly. / Geniebook，《动物的多样性》（小三科学）：哺乳动物有毛发、用肺呼吸，用奶喂养幼仔，大多数是胎生；鸟有羽毛、喙、一对翅膀和一对腿，下硬壳蛋，鸵鸟和企鹅不会飞；鱼有鳞片、鳍和尾巴，用鳃呼吸，大多数下蛋；两栖动物皮肤湿润；爬行动物皮肤干燥、有鳞片，用肺呼吸，有的（如龟）有壳；昆虫有三部分身体、六条腿、两根触角和坚硬的外骨骼；有流程图、给组选标题、找出分错的动物等练习。 (Read 2026-10-21 for the topic's research pass (quotes checked word for word against the page text). A commercial tuition provider's Primary 3 notes, not MOE: used as a picture of what Singapore pupils are taught to look for. Simplifications in these notes are not copied (for example that mould is too small to see, that all fish live in water, or that flowering plants reproduce by spores). / 2026-10-21 研究时读取（引文逐字核对过页面原文）。商业补习机构的小三讲义，不是教育部的材料：用来了解新加坡学生被教导看哪些特征。讲义里过于简化的说法不照抄（比如说霉小到看不见、所有的鱼都住在水里、开花植物用孢子繁殖）。) — https://geniebook.com/tuition/primary-3/science/diversity-of-animals
- [S3] Geniebook, Diversity of Plants (Primary 3 Science): plants make their own food; they are grouped into flowering plants, which can bear flowers, and non-flowering plants, which cannot; flowering plants do not bear flowers all the time; most non-flowering plants reproduce by spores, mainly on the underside of their leaves; non-flowering plants are green too. / Geniebook，《植物的多样性》（小三科学）：植物自己制造食物；分为会开花的开花植物和不会开花的不开花植物；开花植物不是一直都有花；大多数不开花植物用孢子繁殖，孢子主要长在叶背；不开花植物也是绿色的。 (Read 2026-10-21 for the topic's research pass (quotes checked word for word against the page text). The same page's line that every plant has roots, stems and leaves is not used: mosses have no true roots. / 2026-10-21 研究时读取（引文逐字核对过页面原文）。商业补习机构的小三讲义，不是教育部的材料：用来了解新加坡学生被教导看哪些特征。讲义里过于简化的说法不照抄（比如说霉小到看不见、所有的鱼都住在水里、开花植物用孢子繁殖）。同一页说每种植物都有根、茎、叶，这一句不用：苔藓没有真正的根。) — https://geniebook.com/tuition/primary-3/science/diversity-of-plants
- [S4] Geniebook, Fungi & Bacteria (Primary 3 Science): a fungus is not a plant, as it has no roots, stems or leaves, and it cannot make its own food as it has no chlorophyll; examples of fungi are the mushroom, mould and yeast; fungi are decomposers; a bacterium is too small to be seen with the naked eye; some bacteria are good, for example aiding digestion, and some are harmful. / Geniebook，《真菌与细菌》（小三科学）：真菌不是植物，因为它没有根、茎、叶；它没有叶绿素，不能自己制造食物；真菌的例子有蘑菇、霉菌、酵母；真菌是分解者；一个细菌小到肉眼看不见；有的细菌有益，比如帮助消化，有的有害。 (Read 2026-10-21 for the topic's research pass (quotes checked word for word against the page text). - [S5] Geniebook, Living And Non-Living Things (Primary 3 Science): a living thing is also called an organism; plants make their own food while other living things must take in food; some non-living things, such as toy cars, can respond to changes, but non-living things cannot reproduce; classification is grouping things by their characteristics: list the similarities and differences, group, and give each group a suitable heading. / Geniebook，《生物与非生物》（小三科学）：生物也叫有机体；植物自己制造食物，其他生物要吃进食物；有些非生物会对变化作出反应，比如玩具车，但非生物不能繁殖；分类是按特征把东西分组：列出相同和不同之处，分组，再给每组起一个合适的标题。 (Read 2026-10-21 for the topic's research pass (quotes checked word for word against the page text). - [S59] Atlas design study for this topic (docs/38-living-things-content-spec.md §2.8, §3 and §9): a classroom bench 1.9 × 1.1 m drawn life size; a specimen case of 9 × 4 compartments, each 9 cm square, holding 32 model specimens that are not to scale with each other (each fits a 7 cm cell: a dolphin and a guppy take the same space); a sorting tray 1.0 × 0.5 m with felt pads for two, three or six groups; a pad for “none of the six groups” beside the case; yeast cells and bacteria drawn 2,000 times life size on a separate plinth. DESIGN: which features each model shows (the feature table, docs/38 §3.4), following the sources in each specimen’s details; the wording of the yes-or-no questions and the order of the animal flowchart: six legs and three body parts, feathers, hair or fur, fins, scales, moist skin (a design, not MOE’s). SIM, counts in this model: Living or not (seven things): sorted by “moves about by itself”, 4 yes (toy car, grasshopper, squirrel, guppy) and 3 no; by “responds to changes”, 5 yes (with the toy car) and 2 no; by “grows”, “reproduces” or “needs water, food and air”, 4 yes and 3 no (toy car, pebble, plastic flower). Four big groups (13 living things): after 0, 1, 2, 3 questions, 13, 9, 5, 0 left in the case; A plants 4, B animals 4, C fungi 4, D bacteria 1. Plants (six): has flowers now 1 yes, 5 no; flowers, buds or fruits now 2 and 4; needle-like shoots 1 and 5; green 6 and 0; bears flowers at some time 3 and 3. Animals (18): after 0–6 questions, 18, 16, 14, 12, 7, 3, 0 left in the case; A insects 2, B birds 2, C mammals 2, D fins 5 (with the dolphin), E scales 4 (with the pangolin), F moist skin 1, none of these 2 (spider, toad): 3 animals in a group other than their own. A classmate’s tray: 7 wrongly placed, 0 after moving them to the right groups. Which features a model has was decided from the sources cited in its details and from what the model shows: the dolphin is given fins and no hair, because its fins are what can be seen; the pangolin is given scales. The cells on the plinth are drawn at one scale: yeast cells 6 to 9 micrometres across (5–10 µm, S76) and rod-shaped bacteria 2 to 3 micrometres long (0.5–5 µm, S76). / 不是实测，也不是调查：组和件数是分类模型按特征表、针对每个问题算出来的；上面每个件数都有单元测试钉住。每件模型有哪些特征，依据它详情里引用的来源和模型的样子决定：海豚算“有鳍、没有毛发”，因为看得见的是鳍；穿山甲算“有鳞片”。台座上的细胞按同一个比例画：酵母细胞宽 6 到 9 微米（5–10 微米，S76），杆状细菌长 2 到 3 微米（0.5–5 微米，S76）。)

## Numbering

Numbers follow the research register for this topic (docs/38 §6.2: S1 is the syllabus, S2–S74 the research pass of 2026-10-21), so a number means the same source in the spec, the research and here. S59 is the design study (the feature table, the questions and their order, and every count the model gives). S75–S82 were added in the fact check of 2026-10-22 for the items the spec listed as unchecked (§2.7).

Research sources not used, and why: S10 and S11 (common myna: NParks pages contradict each other on whether it is native); S26 (changeable lizard: not on the bench); S37 (banded bull frog: not on the bench); S38 (zebra dove: the page prints the wrong scientific name); S39 (plain tiger: the beetle stands in for the second insect); S44 (tembusu), S52 (resam fern), S53 (spikemoss, neither a moss nor a fern), S54 (a split-gill fungus known only to genus), S74 (crab-eating frog): not on the bench and not needed for the text. S43 and S60–S63 were never assigned.

## Reading limits

- S42 and S76 are Wikipedia, used only for plain definitions and sizes (yeast 5–10 µm, bacteria 0.5–5 µm, a moss's rhizoids, a bat's wing membrane, a dolphin's flukes). S70 is Chinese Wikipedia, used only for the wording of 检索表 and 开花植物.
- S56 was read as an abstract. S57 is a blog reporting exhibition panels; the event itself is S58.
- S8 and some other Singapore Biodiversity Online pages now answer HTTP 410; their text was saved on 2026-10-21.
- NParks words the rain tree's folding leaflets two ways (BiodiversitySG: just before it rains and in the late afternoon; Flora & Fauna Web: in the early evening and on overcast days). The text follows S45 (BiodiversitySG).
- Not found in a reputable source, so not written: that most beetles can fly (only that a beetle flies with its hind wings, S81); scales on a hawksbill's flippers (only on its head, S78); that a dolphin's tail is "horizontal" (the sources say it moves up and down, S76, S77); hair on a pangolin's face and belly.
- Chinese species names: only 黑眶蟾蜍, 疣尾蜥虎, 大蕉松鼠, 马来穿山甲, 许氏齿弹涂鱼, 林八哥 and 孔雀鱼 are names printed by a Singapore agency (Singapore Biodiversity Online). The others (斑鳢, 短耳犬蝠, 斑腿泛树蛙, 网纹蟒, 玳瑁, 龙船花, 木麻黄, 鸟巢蕨, 鹿角蕨, 印度太平洋驼背豚) are common Chinese names, not checked against a Singapore source; they are listed for review in REVIEW.md.
